title: flow-reservoir batcher with KV rebalance and GPU defragmentation for streaming chat
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Design and implement a flow-reservoir batch formation heuristic that continuously forms micro-batches for streaming chat completions while performing KV cache rebalance and opportunistic GPU memory defragmentation. Goal is to reduce 95th-percentile token latency jitter by 20% for streaming flows under mixed priority traffic without increasing overall token cost by more than 5%.

Background: Current continuous batchers favor latency or throughput in isolation and can leave GPU memory fragmented when session KV sizes vary widely. Long-lived conversational sessions cause hot KV slots to persist on a subset of GPUs, reducing effective packing and increasing peak memory pressure. We need a heuristic that: (1) forms batches adaptively from a small flow reservoir that tolerates short waits to assemble low-jitter micro-batches, (2) triggers background KV rebalance to move cold prefixes off hot GPU slabs, and (3) schedules short low-priority defragmentation windows where state is migrated and slabs consolidated without violating latency SLOs for P0/P1 requests.

Success criteria:
- 95th-percentile token latency reduction >= 20% under our mixed synthetic workload (70% streaming chat, 30% short-completion).
- GPU memory peak usage reduction >= 12% on workloads with high KV skew.
- Cost per 1M tokens change within +/-5%.
- No client-facing errors introduced and stable behavior across slow-start and burst scenarios.

Design notes / heuristics: 
1) Flow reservoir: keep a sliding window (reservoir) of open streaming sessions ordered by “urgency score" = weighted sum(epoch age, last-turn-length, priority, entropy of token distribution). Allow a short max-wait (15-30ms tunable) to gather compatible flows into a micro-batch. If urgency score above threshold, bypass wait.

2) Compatibility groups: form micro-batches by (a) similar remaining length and (b) compatible KV affinity (sessions whose KV pages are already colocated). Use a light-weight locality fingerprint (64-bit) to approximate KV slab overlap. Avoid heavy coordination.

3) KV rebalance signal: maintain per-GPU KV heatmap with low-resolution counters. When hotness skew exceeds a tunable ratio (e.g., 3x between top and median), schedule incremental rebalance: migrate low-entropy prefixes (cold pages) off hot GPUs into underutilized GPUs during idle nanowindows in streaming schedule. Migration is incremental and reversible.

4) Opportunistic GPU defragmentation: detect fragmentation via slab free-block fragmentation metric. When fragmentation > threshold and cluster idle budget available (defined by current tail-latency headroom), run short defrag runs that: coalesce small free regions, compact cold KV pages, and update locality fingerprints. Defrag runs are preemptible and bounded (e.g., <= 50ms per run) to avoid SLO violations.

5) Eviction policy integration: extend current TTL/LRU eviction with a "rebalancer score" that prefers migrating cold-but-large prefixes over evicting small-hot pieces that hurt reuse. Also prefer eviction of prefixes with low future-turn probability (from session-history model).

6) Fallbacks and safety: if rebalance/defrag backlog grows or observed latency approaches SLO thresholds, fall back to conservative batching (lower wait, stricter locality) and disable migration until healthy. Provide circuit-breaker metrics and thresholds.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (spike, 2w): implement reservoir sampler + urgency scoring in the batcher; synthetic evaluation harness to measure jitter.
- Phase 2 (3w): add compatibility grouping and lightweight locality fingerprints. Bench on multi-GPU node.
- Phase 3 (4w): implement KV heatmap counters and incremental rebalance prototype; add migration primitives in runtime.
- Phase 4 (3w): defragmentation scheduler with preemption and safety controls; integrate with eviction policy.
- Phase 5 (2w): canary rollout (10% of traffic) with observability and rollback playbook.

Metrics to capture: micro-batch wait distribution, batch size distribution, token latency p50/p95/p99, GPU memory fragmentation metric, KV hotness skew, migration throughput, failed migrations, cost-per-token.

Rollout plan: start with internal QA traffic, then warm canary on non-critical region. Use canary gating: p99 latency change < 1.5x baseline and error rate delta < 0.1%. If safe, expand gradually to 50% then full.

Risks and mitigations:
- Migration causing transient tail spikes: keep migrations small and detect spike quickly; abort if tail rises.
- Incorrect locality fingerprint collisions: make fingerprint conservative (favor false negatives) and validate in canary.
- Increased CPU overhead for bookkeeping: optimize heatmap resolution and sampling cadence, throttle when CPU pressure high.

Open questions:
- Exact urgency score weights (need empirical tuning).
- Tradeoff curve between wait budget and token cost at different traffic mixes.
- Best migration granularity for our slab allocator.

Artifacts: design doc in Confluence, microbench harness under repo serving/runtime/batcher-experiments, and perf dashboards for canary.
